related.name: Free-Space Path Loss & Link Budget Calculator

method: Models a single constant-rate voice stream. Payload per packet is the codec rate in kb/s multiplied by the packet time in milliseconds and divided by eight, which is exact for the codecs offered: G.711 and G.722 at 64 kb/s, G.726-32 at 32 kb/s and G.729 at 8 kb/s. Packet time must be a whole number of milliseconds from 5 to 120; G.729 carries a 10 ms frame, so its packet time must be a multiple of 10 and at least 10. Header bytes are 12 for RTP (no contributing source list and no header extension), 8 for UDP and 20 for IPv4 or 40 for IPv6; layer 2 adds 18 bytes for the Ethernet header and frame check sequence, or 38 when the 8-byte preamble and 12-byte inter-frame gap are counted as well, and the layer-3 view adds none. Packets per second is 1000 divided by the packet time; the layer-3 rate is the payload plus headers times 8 times that packet rate, the wire rate adds the layer-2 bytes, and the bidirectional figure is twice the wire rate. Overhead share is the header and layer-2 bytes divided by the whole frame, and it classifies the result as below 50 percent, from 50 to 70 percent, and above 70 percent. The call count is the link capacity in Mb/s times one million divided by the bidirectional per-call rate, rounded down, so a call that does not fit returns zero; the same capacity is also evaluated for G.711 at the same packet time and framing so the codec difference is visible. Inputs: packet time 5 to 120 ms, capacity 0.1 to 100000 Mb/s, four codecs, two IP versions and three framing choices; anything else is refused with the field named rather than coerced. The model excludes silence suppression, RTP header compression, SRTP authentication and encryption bytes, retransmission, signalling, jitter-buffer delay, codec lookahead, traffic mix, queueing and variable-rate codecs such as Opus, whose payload size depends on the encoder setting. It reports a link budget, not a measurement of a live network. Pure local arithmetic: no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: RFC 3550, RTP: A Transport Protocol for Real-Time Applications — the fixed 12-byte RTP header and the real-time transport model.
RFC 3551, RTP Profile for Audio and Video Conferences with Minimal Control — static payload types and packetisation for G.711, G.722 and G.729.
ITU-T G.711 and G.729 — 64 kb/s and 8 kb/s speech codecs, their frame durations and their payload sizes.
IEEE 802.3, Ethernet — frame header, frame check sequence, preamble and inter-frame gap accounting.
